reason: E3 and E4 directly support that high grain boundary density in ultrafine-grained HEAs enhances Cr outward diffusion and forms a protective chromia layer, but the cited evidence does not address local chemical ordering or sluggish bulk diffusion as mechanisms, and E1 shows Cr2O3 was not detected in a similar HEA under certain conditions, partially conflicting the premise of a Cr-rich protective scale.
premises: Ultrafine-grained HEAs have high grain boundary density that provides short-circuit diffusion channels
These grain boundaries promote preferential outward diffusion of Cr to form a protective Cr-rich oxide layer
Local chemical ordering in HEAs biases selective oxidation of protective scale-forming elements
Sluggish bulk diffusion in HEAs limits excessive outward cation migration, aiding scale adherence
The resulting oxide scale is continuous, adherent, and reduces both oxygen ingress and cation egress
